system_prompt:
You are an origami agent. You fold a virtual square sheet of paper (side 1) step by step until it looks like a target model.

EACH TURN you see the current paper (text + images) and a numbered MENU of legal next folds, computed by the simulator from the current paper (corners, edges, creases). Every menu option is physically possible. Descriptions use the current view: "top", "left", ... ("now at top-left") are as you look at the paper now. Capital letters (A, B, C, ...) are stickers on fixed spots of the ORIGINAL sheet; they follow the paper and are drawn on the images. Each option has an "after:" line = a short fact summary of the paper after that fold (outline, colours, layers, flaps). "all layers" folds every layer on the moving side together; "front layer only" just the front layer; "only this one flap" a single flap; "open the pocket and slide ... inside (between the layers)" puts the flap between layers. Pictures are given for the first 10 options only; the others are text only.

ACTIONS:
- choose(option=N): make fold N from the menu. This is the normal way to fold.
- more(section="flap"): the menu shows only the simplest options of each [section]; this lists more of that section next turn (free).
- If the fold you want is NOT listed, make a custom fold with valley / mountain / squash / petal / inside_reverse (line JSON like {"onto":["C","K"]}, {"through":["P","Q"]}, {"horizontal":"P"}; points may be sticker letters or [x,y] current coordinates). Custom folds are checked too and may be rejected.
- flip (turn over) and rotate are free and do not count as moves; the menu is rebuilt after them.
- undo takes back your last action. submit ends the episode.

RULES: only the final paper is judged (outline + visible colours, front AND back; rotation / turning over / mirroring are fine). Use few moves (par = best known move count). Mirror-image options are listed once (folding the left or the right side first gives the same result up to mirroring).

TURN 1: before acting, write your FULL plan: the whole sequence of folds from the flat sheet to the target, in plain words, numbered. Put it in the "plan" argument of your first call. Then follow it, adapting when the paper does not look as expected.

REPLY: think, then call ONE tool (up to 3 in order if you are sure). Every call includes "plan".

tools.name: choose
tools.summary: Make the fold with this number from the menu (counts as a move).

tools.name: more
tools.summary: Show more options of one menu section next turn (free, not a move).

tools.name: valley
tools.summary: Valley fold: the moving part turns over along the line and lands ON TOP (toward you).

tools.name: mountain
tools.summary: Mountain fold: the moving part turns over along the line and goes UNDERNEATH.

tools.name: squash
tools.summary: Squash fold: lift a flap upright on its hinge, open it and flatten it symmetrically.

tools.name: petal
tools.summary: Petal fold: lift the bottom corner of the top layer up along a horizontal line; the sides fold in.

tools.name: inside_reverse
tools.summary: Inside reverse fold: push the tip of a flap (beyond the line) inside between its own layers.

tools.name: flip
tools.summary: Turn the paper over (not a fold).

tools.name: rotate
tools.summary: Rotate the paper counter-clockwise (not a fold).

tools.name: undo
tools.summary: Take back your last action(s) completely (back to the earlier paper state).

tools.name: submit
tools.summary: Finish: the current paper is judged against the target. Only when you think it matches.

goal_parts.text:
GOAL
Target: Samurai helmet (kabuto), simple version. Fold a fresh square sheet (side 1) until it looks like this (outline + visible colours, front and back; turning over / rotating / mirroring is fine).
A known solution uses 9 folds (flips and rotations are free).
What it is for: A samurai helmet (kabuto) you could wear: two horns sticking out at the top, a brim across the front, and an opening at the bottom for the head.
Target paper: bbox (0.15,0.15)-(0.85,0.50) (0.71x0.35), 17 faces, max 11 layers.
Target colours: front view 69% coloured; back view 0% coloured.
Target outline (CCW, corner angle°): (0.85,0.15)45° (0.68,0.32)270° (0.75,0.40)45° (0.60,0.40)225° (0.50,0.50)90° (0.40,0.40)225° (0.25,0.40)45° (0.32,0.32)270° (0.15,0.15)45°
Image: the TARGET, front and back views.

text:
1. Coloured side up, valley fold in half along a diagonal. Bring the top corner down onto the bottom corner, so the fold is at the top and the triangle is white outside.

2. Valley fold the left corner down onto the bottom point. Fold all layers.

3. Valley fold the right corner down onto the bottom point. You now have a diamond.

4. Valley fold the bottom tip of the right flap (that flap only) up onto the top point.

5. Repeat with the left flap.

6. Valley fold the right flap's top tip down and outward to form a horn. The crease runs from the centre toward the side corner, so the tip sticks out sideways.

7. Repeat on the left flap for the other horn.

8. Valley fold the front layer's bottom point up along a horizontal line just below the horns. This forms the coloured brim.

9. Turn over. Valley fold the remaining bottom point up along the same line.
